datasets.title: Iraq: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/irq-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values from VIIRS satellite observations are collected at 10-day intervals and processed into raster composites. FAPAR anomalies are calculated at each grid cell as the deviation from a long-term mean baseline (2012 to the last available full year), enabling detection and monitoring of agricultural drought impacts on vegetation growth and productivity across Iraq.

sources.name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS)
sources.description: FAPAR and FAPAR anomaly datasets derived from Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) satellite observations, processed by the European Commission Joint Research Centre to provide 10-day composite vegetation indices for drought monitoring
